slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Single slot, no backup/mirror and no generation counter. Load acceptance: 8-byte magic OK, 4-byte version OK, checksum_sum32 OK, checksum_condneg OK (FUN_080072a4 errors 1-4 in that order); load retried up to 3 times by FUN_08007244. Save writes all 64 blocks then read-back-verifies each block (FUN_0800712c/FUN_0805a23c), retried up to 3 times by FUN_080071d4. NOTE: offsets in this file are RAM-image offsets; the raw .sav file stores each 8-byte block byte-reversed: sav_offset = (ram_offset & ~7) | (7 - (ram_offset & 7)).

checksums.name: checksum_sum32_le
checksums.formula_detail: acc = sum of the 126 little-endian u32 words at RAM offsets 0x000..0x1F7 (504 bytes), modulo 2^32. Stored u32_le at RAM 0x1F8, immediately past the covered range (no self-reference). In the raw .sav file the stored word appears block-reversed inside the final 8-byte block. Computed by FUN_08007320, stamped on every save by FUN_0800712c, verified on every load by FUN_080072a4 (error 3 on mismatch).

checksums.name: checksum_condneg
checksums.formula_detail: Order-dependent conditional-negation sum over the same 126 little-endian u32 words at RAM 0x000..0x1F7: acc=0; for each word x: if (x <= acc, unsigned) x = (-x) mod 2^32; acc = (acc + x) mod 2^32. Stored u32_le at RAM 0x1FC. Computed by FUN_08007358, stamped on every save by FUN_0800712c, verified on every load by FUN_080072a4 (error 4 on mismatch). Independent of checksum_sum32_le; both must be repaired after any edit. Sample values are RAM-image-decoded (after 8-byte block-reversal transform of the raw .sav).

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 transfer primitive: programs DMA3 SAD/DAD/CNT (register group at 0x040000D4), sets enable bit 0x80000000, busy-waits on control bit 0x8000. Used for both directions (src/dst swapped by caller). Not erase; EEPROM has no erase command in this driver.

EEPROM read of one 8-byte block: bounds-checks addr against descriptor+4, DMAs address/read frame to 0x0D000000 (count = addr_bits+3), DMAs 0x44 halfword samples back, reassembles 4 u16 from low bits and stores them to dst+6,+4,+2,+0 (descending - source of the block-reversal file mapping).

EEPROM write of one 8-byte block: expands 4 u16 into a 64-bit serial frame plus address bits and start/stop bits, DMAs addr_bits+0x43 halfwords to 0x0D000000, calls FUN_08059f54 write-enable, polls EEPROM line 0x0D000000 bit 0 for ready, calls FUN_08059fdc teardown. Sole EEPROM writer.

Write-enable / bus-setup helper: programs a control block from a 3-u16 argument (passed via 0x0805a230 literal) and sets channel bit 8<<type. Internal register identities unresolved in the exported literals.
Bus-teardown helper: clears the control block and channel bit set by FUN_08059f54 after the write ready-poll completes.

Read-back verify of one 8-byte block: re-reads via FUN_0805a0a0 and compares 4 u16 against RAM; returns 0 on match, 0x8000 on mismatch. This is the save's only redundancy mechanism - there is no backup copy.

EEPROM type/descriptor select (called with type=3 by both save and load; type>3 is an error, reported as error 5). Descriptor supplies total block count at +4 (u16 loop bound) and serial address-bit width at +8 (u8). Descriptor literal values not exported.
Checksum 1: sum of 126 u32_le words over RAM 0x000..0x1F7.
Checksum 2: conditional-negation sum over the same 126 u32_le words (negate word when word <= running accumulator).

Save-all: stamps both checksums at RAM+0x1F8/+0x1FC, writes blocks 0..count-1 via FUN_0805a158, then verifies each block via FUN_0805a23c. The RAM struct is the EEPROM image verbatim (no packing); the only fields it mutates are the two checksums.
Load-all: selects descriptor via FUN_08059f1c(3) then fills the whole RAM struct block-by-block via FUN_0805a0a0. No field-level parsing.
Magic-1 validation: byte-compares 8 bytes at struct base against ROM string (proved to be 'mobile21'); returns 1 on mismatch.
Post-load validator, strict order: magic1 (error 1), version '0.05' at base+8 (error 2), checksum1 vs +0x1F8 (error 3), checksum2 vs +0x1FC (error 4), else 0 = valid.
Save retry wrapper: calls FUN_0800712c up to 3 times while it returns non-zero. No caller recovered (game dispatch via unrecovered jumptables).
Load retry wrapper: up to 3 attempts of FUN_080071f0 read-all followed by FUN_080072a4 validation. No caller recovered (game dispatch via unrecovered jumptables).

caller_chains.trigger_context: Game save operation (exact gameplay trigger not recoverable: no caller above the retry wrapper exists in callgraph.json or decompiled.c because dispatch uses unrecovered jumptables). Retried up to 3 times on any failure.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Direct calls in decompiled.c: FUN_080071d4 loops on FUN_0800712c; FUN_0800712c stores FUN_08007320/FUN_08007358 results at base+0x1F8/base+0x1FC, calls FUN_08059f1c(3,...), then FUN_0805a158(block, base+block*8) for all blocks and FUN_0805a23c for verification. Cross-checked against callgraph.json edges 0805a158->{08059f54,08059fdc,0805a020} and 0805a23c->0805a0a0. Payload fields are NOT mutated by this chain - they must already be in RAM, written by untraced gameplay code.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Save load at boot / continue (exact dispatch not recoverable, as above). Up to 3 attempts; an attempt succeeds only if read-all and full validation both pass.
ram_fields_updated: 0x000-0x1FF entire RAM save struct overwritten from EEPROM by FUN_080071f0/FUN_0805a0a0
caller_chains.how_mapped: Direct calls in decompiled.c: FUN_08007244 loops {FUN_080071f0, FUN_080072a4}; FUN_080071f0 calls FUN_08059f1c(3,...) then FUN_0805a0a0(block, base+block*8) for all blocks; FUN_080072a4 calls FUN_08007268 (magic), compares base+8 version, then FUN_08007320/FUN_08007358 against base+0x1F8/base+0x1FC. Cross-checked against callgraph.json edge 0805a0a0->0805a020.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Read-back verification phase of every save, after the write loop completes without error.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Second loop in FUN_0800712c decompiled body; FUN_0805a23c is listed in callgraph.json with callee 0x0805a0a0 and caller 0x0800712c in save_related_functions.c header. Compares EEPROM contents against the RAM struct without modifying it.

fields.name: magic_mobile21
fields.update_mechanism: Compared byte-by-byte on every load (validator error 1 on mismatch). Not written by any traced save/load function; stamped at save creation by code outside the recovered corpus.
fields.evidence: FUN_08007268 8-byte compare called by FUN_080072a4; RAM-decoded cap-01 bytes 0x00-0x07 are exactly 'mobile21' (raw file shows block-reversed '12elibom'). Absolute RAM base unresolved: Ghidra _DAT literal values were not exported, so ram_addr is null rather than guessed.

fields.name: format_version
fields.update_mechanism: Compared on every load at struct base+8 (validator error 2 on mismatch). Acts as a format-version gate independent of the checksums.
fields.evidence: FUN_080072a4 compares 4 bytes at base+8 against a ROM string; RAM-decoded cap-01 bytes 0x08-0x0B are '0.05' (raw file bytes 0x0C-0x0F read '50.0' due to block reversal).

fields.name: header_sentinel_0x0c
fields.update_mechanism: No traced reader or writer. Fixed 0xFFFFFFFF in the only populated sample; presumed reserved/sentinel. Any edit requires full checksum repair and a reload test (fuzzing target).
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 bytes 0x0C-0x0F; absence of any reference in decompiled.c validation or transfer code.

fields.name: zero_region_0x10
fields.update_mechanism: Copied verbatim by load/save block transfers; semantics, if any, are in untraced gameplay code. Zero in this early save - unset payload and reserved space are indistinguishable from one sample.
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 bytes 0x10-0x3F are all zero; no traced function interprets them.

fields.name: table_header_0x40
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown. Candidate count/header halfword for the following 9-entry table; only fuzzing (set to 1/9/10 with checksum repair) can confirm or refute.
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 u16 at 0x40 is 0x0000 while the next nine u16 all hold 30000.

fields.name: default_table_0x42
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; never written by the traced save path. Nine identical values of 30000 have the shape of unset defaults in a fixed-size table (scores/times/records), but no reader in the corpus interprets them.
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 u16[9] at 0x42..0x53 all equal 0x7530; type is an array of nine u16_le (schema type enum has no array form, so recorded as u16_le with the count in the name/evidence).

fields.name: table_tail_0x54
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; trailing zero halfwords of the 0x40-0x57 region, either further genuinely-zero table entries or padding.
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 u16 at 0x54 and 0x56 are both 0x0000.

fields.name: zero_region_0x58
fields.update_mechanism: Copied verbatim by block transfers; semantics unknown (see zero_region_0x10).
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 bytes 0x58-0x7F are all zero.

fields.name: region_0x80_header
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; zero head of the second structured region (0x80-0x9F).

fields.name: payload_0x84
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; never written by the traced save path. Four distinct small bytes suggest packed sub-fields (counters/flags) rather than one integer. Primary semantics fuzzing target: flip each byte with full checksum repair and observe gameplay/UI.
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 bytes 0x84-0x87; the only non-trivial payload bytes outside the header and the 0x42 table.

fields.name: sentinel_0x88
fields.update_mechanism: No traced reader or writer. Mirrors the 0x0C sentinel; possibly an empty-record marker (-1) inside the 0x80 region.
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 bytes 0x88-0x8B are 0xFF; no reference in traced code.

fields.name: zero_region_0x8c
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; zero space between the 0x88 sentinel and the 0x9F flag byte.
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 bytes 0x8C-0x9E are all zero.

fields.name: flag_0x9f
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown. Lone trailing 0x01 at the end of the 32-byte 0x80 region; candidate valid/count flag for that region. Toggle 0x01<->0x00 with checksum repair to test.
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 byte 0x9F is 0x01 with all of 0x8C-0x9E zero.

fields.name: zero_region_0xa0
fields.update_mechanism: Copied verbatim by block transfers. Largest candidate home for progression/inventory state that is simply unset in this early save; nothing in the corpus distinguishes its sub-regions.
fields.evidence: RAM-decoded cap-01 bytes 0xA0-0x1F7 are all zero (344 bytes).

fields.name: checksum_sum32_le
fields.update_mechanism: Recomputed by FUN_08007320 and stamped by FUN_0800712c on every save over RAM 0x000-0x1F7; verified by FUN_080072a4 on every load (error 3). Stored in the raw file block-reversed within the final block (file 0x1FC-0x1FF region).
fields.evidence: Python verification on RAM-decoded cap-01: computed 0x1bb6dfd0 == stored 0x1bb6dfd0. Blank cap-00 correctly mismatches (0xffffff82 vs 0xffffffff). Absolute RAM address is base+0x1F8; the base literal was not exported, so ram_addr is null.

fields.name: checksum_condneg
fields.update_mechanism: Recomputed by FUN_08007358 and stamped by FUN_0800712c on every save over RAM 0x000-0x1F7; verified by FUN_080072a4 on every load (error 4). Must be repaired together with checksum_sum32_le after any edit.
fields.evidence: Python verification on RAM-decoded cap-01: computed 0x762fd3c6 == stored 0x762fd3c6. Blank cap-00 correctly mismatches (0x00000000 vs 0xffffffff).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one byte of magic 'mobile21' (RAM 0x00), repair both checksums
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Load rejected with validator error 1 after 3 retries; game behaves as if no save exists. Proves magic is gated independently of checksums.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change version '0.05' to '0.06' (RAM 0x08-0x0B), repair both checksums
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Load rejected with validator error 2. Proves the version gate is a real compatibility check.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one byte at RAM 0x84 WITHOUT checksum repair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Load rejected with validator error 3 (checksum_sum32 is checked before checksum_condneg). Negative control for all other tests.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one byte at RAM 0x84, repair checksum_sum32_le only
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Load rejected with validator error 4. Proves both checksums are independent mandatory gates.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip each byte of RAM 0x84-0x87 in separate runs (values 0x00/0x01/0xFF), repair both checksums
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Load succeeds (error 0). Any changed counter/flag/unlock/display localises the semantics of the 0x80-0x9F region.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set first u16 of the 0x42 table from 30000 to 1, then 0, then 65535 in separate runs; repair both checksums
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the nine 30000 values are per-entry defaults (scores/times/records), exactly one entry changes in UI/gameplay; identifies per-entry semantics.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set u16 at RAM 0x40 to 1, 9, 10 in separate runs; repair both checksums
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Tests the count/header hypothesis for the 0x42 table: a listing that shows that many entries (or garbage/crash at 10) confirms; no change refutes.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Clear sentinel RAM 0x88-0x8B to 00 00 00 00 (second run: clear 0x0C-0x0F); repair both checksums
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Load must still succeed (no traced reader). A record appearing/disappearing promotes the sentinel hypothesis; no change keeps it reserved.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Toggle flag byte RAM 0x9F between 0x01 and 0x00; repair both checksums
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If 0x9F is a valid/count flag for the 0x80 region, the corresponding feature/record toggles; correlate with the 0x84 tests.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Write 0x01 to a single zero-region byte, one run each at RAM 0x10, 0x58, 0xA0, 0x100, 0x180, 0x1F0; repair both checksums
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Load succeeds. Any gameplay-visible change discovers a live field in the zero space and refutes 'reserved' for that area.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Store checksum_sum32_le big-endian at RAM 0x1F8 (deliberately wrong endianness)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Load rejected with validator error 3. Falsification test confirming little-endian storage.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Patch the RAW FILE bytes at file offset 0x08-0x0B instead of RAM 0x08-0x0B (bypassing the block-reversal transform); repair both checksums in RAM space
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Save still loads with the original version, because file 0x08-0x0B maps to RAM 0x0F-0x0C. A version change here would falsify the block-reversal model.

open_questions: What is the absolute RAM base address (0x02xxxxxx/0x03xxxxxx) of the 512-byte save struct? The Ghidra export omits _DAT literal-pool values, so ram_addr is null for every field and gameplay writers cannot be cross-referenced by address.

Which gameplay functions write the payload fields (RAM 0x10-0x1F7) before a save, and what are the semantics of the 0x42 nine-entry 30000-default table, the 0x84-0x87 bytes, the 0x88/0x0C sentinels, and the 0x9F flag byte? No such writer is identifiable in this corpus; only fuzzing with checksum repair (see fuzzing_targets) or a fuller decompilation with resolved literals can answer this.
What code initialises the 'mobile21'/'0.05' magics when a new save is created? No traced function writes them.

What are the numeric values in the type-3 EEPROM descriptor (block count at +4, address-bit width at +8)? Their roles are proven and 64 blocks is proven by the 512-byte file, but the descriptor bytes themselves were not exported.

What are the register-level identities inside FUN_08059f54/FUN_08059fdc (write-enable/teardown)? Their position in the write sequence is proven; their internal register semantics are not resolvable from the exported literals.

Who calls the top-level wrappers FUN_080071d4 (save) and FUN_08007244 (load), i.e. what gameplay events trigger a save? Callgraph edges above them are missing because dispatch returns through unrecovered jumptables.
Is FUN_080070b4/FUN_08059eb4(4) related to save-media probing at boot? It has no traced edge into the save/load chain and is recorded as tangential only.

Do the large zero regions (especially RAM 0xA0-0x1F7, 344 bytes) hold progression/inventory fields that are merely unset in this single early populated sample? A later-game save sample would resolve most of the UNKNOWN field rows at once.
